newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds get late boost from strong Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Bunds get late boost from strong Treasuries.

text.p: Bunds tested the top-side of their recent range on Wednesday, slavishly following Treasuries higher late in a day lacking any meaningful domestic news.

Traders said they expect the market to continue stuck in Treasury-led ranges on Thursday with no market-moving events scheduled other than a meeting between German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and French President Jacques Chirac tonight.
At 1356 GMT, the DTB June Bund futures contract was up 41 basis points at 100.59, near its high for the day and well off an early low of 100.16.
"There is not too much going on domestically to explain the gains," said Catherine Lee, analyst at R.H. Wrightson & Associates. "There is nothing going on this week."
She and others said they doubt that Kohl and Chirac will say anything market-moving this evening, likely only repeating well-worn comments about their determination to start monetary union on time.

Although pro-EMU statements have recently benefited high-yielding bond markets, Bunds have felt little impact. Analysts said Bund traders are still nervous that EMU could hold an inflation threat for German debt.
Although the market's mood is fairly neutral, traders said they see a risk that Bunds could break out of the recent range to the downside.
Upcoming economic German data, they argue, could show the economy picking up speed, raising fears of inflation.
Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said the economy probably grew in the first quarter, but that the pace of expansion must speed up if growth of 2.5 percent is to be reached this year.
The spread between Bunds and Treasuries meanwhile was steady around 111 basis points.

Analysts said they do not see much more room for the spread against Treasuries to widen. The spread has already widened considerably and both the German and U.S. economies appear to be picking up speed, they said.
The yield curve was also steady on the day with the spread between two- and 10-year maturities unchanged at 226 basis points.
The benchmark cash 10-year Bund was stronger late in the day, climbing in price to 100.81 from 100.68 with the yield falling to 5.88 percent.
